Enterprise Integration Patterns

Message Channel

by Gregor Hohpe

When two applications need to exchange information, they connect via a Message Channel. The sending application places information into the channel; the receiving application reads it from the channel.

A Message Channel is a logical pathway — often implemented over a message broker — that decouples the sender from the receiver in time and space.

Problem

How can two applications communicate reliably without requiring that both be available at the same time?

Solution

Use a Message Channel. The sending application puts the message on the channel and continues; the receiving application consumes it when ready.
